RAFF4, RAFF3, T1ρ, T2ρ, and MTI are able to identify changes in T2-weighted defined normally appearing white matter, but that RAFF4 and T1ρ are the only ones that can be used in the presence of gadolinium-based contrast agent.

RAFF4, and possibly also T1ρ and/or T2ρ, are sensitive to slow motion and may be able to detect changes within T2w-defined white matter of patients, but that their use as biomarkers for monitoring MS disease activity and treatment response is not yet fully validated.

RAFF4, and T1ρ are sensitive to the same pathological processes as T2 and T2* and that they can be used as markers of diffuse WM abnormalities in patients with MS, but that RAFF4 is also sensitive to the presence of lesions, which may explain the differences in the results obtained with RAFF4 and T1ρ in patients with relapsing-remitting MS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the T1ρ and the RAFF4 relaxations are sensitive markers of diffuse white-matter abnormalities in MS, and they may be used to assess the effects of treatment.
RAFF4, and T1ρ and to a lesser extent T2ρ, are sensitive to slow motonal regimes in the normal appearing white matter of MS patients and may be useful in detecting changes in this tissue.
RAFF4, and to a lesser extent T1ρ, are promising MRI markers of white matter abnormalities in MS, which could be used in clinical trials and for monitoring disease activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of RAFF4, in addition to T1ρ, T2ρ and T2w MRI, can help in the detection and monitoring of diffuse white matter changes in multiple sclerosis.

T1ρ, RAFF4 and T2ρ are sensitive to changes in the white matter of patients affected by multiple sclerosis, even in regions with no evidence of T2-weighted abnormalities, and that these changes are independent of the alterations in the functional connectivity metrics.
